about: What tools/build_latest.ps1 builds: the newest playable state. The orchestrator keeps this current as branches land; every listed merge is checked to be conflict-free when it changes. Branch names are without origin/; paths are relative to unity/.
contents: The farmland preview at physics model 102: two nights of physics in the player, on the Play build (Play opens two maps, House and Village; M opens the world's map). Everything recently built is merged in at the pilot's word, the parts not fully tested too (D-113). New since the model 100 build: the physics steps are faster where they froze or crawled (the laid fiber's checks against a ruin's many boxes, and the wind's sheltering map rebuilt on four threads instead of one: the freezes of 0.1 to 1.4 s), with every result unchanged; a drone's parts no longer pass through a wire's cable at speed (model 101); and the fiber no longer breaks where it wraps thin boards and slabs, as in the ruins, and wood, bark and fabric wear it only mildly (model 102: all eight of the pilot's flights that broke that way keep their line when re-flown on their own sticks). New since model 85. Straw, tall grass and tree crowns act on the props: a blade cuts a stem only where it is fast enough, each cut takes work from the rotor and pushes its arm, and the summary names what each rotor cut (how many stems, of what, for how many joules); a drone in a crown falls through the twigs with the props turning and cutting, and rests only on a branch or the ground. The legs are the hand-made ones: each of the four has its own stiffness, drawn from the flight's seed and written in the log; a leg cracks, sets, kinks, folds and tears by its tube's own law, and a broken half hangs from its neighbour and lies on the ground instead of in it. The contact bug that tumbled cut landings on 10 to 20 degree slopes is fixed (a foot's hold stretched by metres). A fast prop meets a thin branch or a wire instead of passing through it. The wind takes the farmland's groves, hedges and thin ruin walls for what they are, and its gusts now scale with height: near the ground they are smaller and quicker, as the air's are there (model 100, new in this build and the least tested part of it). The drone's own rotor wake shakes it at its measured level (at most 6.2 % of the hover's thrust either way, less in cruise), and a descent through its own wash moves the thrust both ways. The fiber turns at the canister's exit as on a point, a resting line is held instead of thrown, the rotors' wash reaches the ground from any height, and the line lying under the drone moves in it. Everything else is as in the Play build: Village's hills, trees, bushes and ruins solid, the wind over the hills, the friend's look, the analog feed, the OSD, the motors, the failsafe, R, C, X, V, pause, Explore in noclip, the summary and the flight log. Known, being fixed (D-114): a full-stick turn-around can put the line into a prop because the spool's pull is drawn too heavy; it can still slip through a 2 mm twig late in a long wrap; the physics still runs slower than it should in the game (the game's runtime costs 3 to 5 times the test tools'), so it can still feel sluggish when the line lies on a ruin. Known, not judged yet: a leg cracks from 0.3 m/s of sideways drift at touchdown and most break or bend at 0.6 m/s, and on a kerb the damage jumps from none at 1.25 m/s to three or four legs at 1.5 m/s; a conductor met at the frame now stops the drone hard (the clamp's own failure and the wire's give are not modelled). Known: a very sharp liftoff or a low move back over the laid line does not cut the fiber on the props yet (it hangs on how the line lies at launch: a question for the pilot); dry ground almost never holds a leg's foot; the hull's turning moment in a crosswind is measured but not flown; straw under the drone folds by the plain column of air (the wash with distance is built for it and switched off); on House a landing on a trench's soil can sink in; the frame rate was measured on the Play build and not again on this one (111 fps through the feed in the laptop's Performance mode, about 60 in Quiet mode); the fiber's dragged corner at a sharp low turn was not measured again; the props in the frame are still the still ones (the turning props are built and wait for the camera's move, D-103); our trenches, houses and cars are not in Village yet (W5, half built); the open map covers the OSD's centre; on House's map the houses are only about 10 px across; a pine's thick arms are needle cards and still flutter.
